sections.title: Definition & Overview
sections.content: PDR is defined by the presence of neovascularization elsewhere (NVE) or neovascularization of the disc (NVD) due to profound retinal ischemia. It marks the shift from non-proliferative retinopathy to a state where VEGF-driven vessel growth threatens permanent vision loss via hemorrhage and tractional retinal detachment.

sections.title: Pathophysiology: The VEGF Cascade
content: 1. Chronic Hyperglycemia causes pericyte loss.
2. Capillary occlusion leads to peripheral retinal ischemia.
3. Ischemic retina releases VEGF and Angiopoietin-2.
4. VEGF stimulates pathological angiogenesis.
5. Neovascular membranes form on the retina/disc.

sections.title: Clinical Features
content: Sudden painless vision loss (VH)
Floaters (small hemorrhages)
Peripheral vision loss (advanced tractional RD)
Severe glare (due to dense fibrosis)

sections.title: Red Flags: Immediate Intervention
content: NVD > 1/3 disc area
Presence of Vitreous Hemorrhage
Tractional Retinal Detachment (TRD) involving macula
Rubeosis iridis (Iris neovascularization)

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup
content: 1. Dilated Fundus Exam: Essential for identifying NVD/NVE.
2. Fluorescein Angiography (FFA): Highlights leakage and capillary non-perfusion zones.
3. SD-OCT: Assess for macular edema (DME) and membrane traction.
4. B-Scan Ultrasonography: Mandatory if view is obscured by hemorrhage to rule out TRD.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: PRP remains the gold standard for long-term control of high-risk PDR.
Anti-VEGF as monotherapy requires strict compliance; high risk of loss to follow-up.
Always evaluate the fellow eye; symmetry of disease is common.
In pregnancy, PDR can progress rapidly; monitor every trimester.

sections.title: Recent Advances
sections.content: The Protocol S study (DRCR Retina Network) established that anti-VEGF (Aflibercept) is non-inferior to PRP for PDR at 2 years, with better visual acuity outcomes in patients with concurrent DME. However, PRP is still preferred in patients with poor follow-up compliance due to the 'safety net' effect.
